PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality wide-moat franchise, but the current risk-reward is unfavorable across all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals/trajectory): While YoY growth remains positive (revenue +7.4%, EPS +5.8%), the sequential deterioration is severe — operating margin compressed 460bps in two quarters (26.2% → 21.6%), EPS declined -16.4% peak-to-trough sequentially, and QoQ OCF fell -18.6%. The margin compression is accelerating and likely oil-driven (WTI at $100.20, +50.9% in 90 days), with management quantifying a ~$1B after-tax annualized oil headwind for FY2027 and a $400M tariff headwind for FY2026. Guidance is biased to the lower end of $6.83–$7.09 core EPS. Pillar 2 (valuation): PE at 22.5x is near the 1-year floor of 21.7x, but the earnings yield of 4.4% is essentially equal to the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%, meaning zero equity-risk premium for a decelerating consumer-staples business. The multiple compression is justified by the earnings trajectory, not a buying opportunity. P/B at 6.7x is similarly at the low end of its 6.4–7.9 range. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): There is no credible near-term re-rating catalyst — management is declining FY2027 guidance until July, the restructuring ($1.5B COGS savings) is a two-year program, and the next earnings event will likely show continued margin pressure from sustained oil prices above $100. The volume inflection (2% in Q3) and innovation traction (Tide evo) are genuine positives but insufficient to offset the cost headwinds and zero valuation cushion. The stock is fairly priced for deteriorating fundamentals, not mispriced.
